_comment: Policy for the PRO-179 world-DB updater pre-flight gate.
Every value here is a governance decision owned by Scuff (SQL) and reviewed by Scuff (Rev).
Fail-closed rule: a table that is not listed in 'tables' (base tables) or 'customTables'
cannot be written by a company-authored update file. Adding a table = a reviewed diff to this file.
Bands come from docs/content-playbook.md section 2.4 (reserved ids) and PRO-175 (spawn-guid band).
PRO-248 (PRO-179 review NB-E). The write-policy exemption for an origin:upstream
directory is a claim about history, and `git commit --author="Someone
<x@azerothcore.org>" data/sql/updates/db_world/x.sql` is enough to make that
claim locally. So a new file in an upstream-tagged directory is only exempt when
it also exists in verifiedRef — with the bytes that ref holds for it, not just the
name — the ref the tree is tracking. A forged --author
does not put the file in the ref; a `git pull` does.
verifiedRef must name a remote-tracking ref (refs/remotes/...): a local branch is
writable by the very person the rule constrains, and pointing it at HEAD would
make every file look upstream. Write it fully qualified: the short name
`origin/Playerbot` is ambiguous the moment anyone runs `git branch origin/Playerbot
HEAD`, and git then reads refs/heads/origin/Playerbot while refusing to say which
ref it meant — `git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name` answers with nothing. The gate
treats that unanswered question as 'not remote-tracking' and refuses the boot
(PRO-248 review B1) rather than defaulting to the exemption. It is read with local
object database lookups only — nothing here fetches, so an ordinary offline boot
still resolves it.
States: verified -> exempt as before (a match that only holds modulo case is exempt
but WARNed as upstream-ref-case-divergence). unverified -> FAIL naming the pending
directory, because company content belongs in pending_db_world; a name that is in
the ref whose bytes are not is FAILed as unverified-upstream-content. indeterminate
(git could not answer, or verifiedRef is not under refs/remotes/) -> FAIL, failing
closed, naming refreshCommand.
unchecked (ref not configured or not present locally) -> WARN naming
refreshCommand and the pre-PRO-248 dir+author exemption is kept: refusing every
clone that has never fetched is worse than the status quo, and the report says so.
Deleting this block, emptying verifiedRef, or moving verifiedRef out of
refs/remotes/ is a governance change to a reviewed file, not a way to pass:
ops/preflight/audit_policy_schema.py exits 1 on all three.

creature._comment: guid is the primary key and the reserved spawn band; (id1, map) is allowed as an alternative key because a content file legitimately re-spawns its own template, and id1 is itself band-checked. id2/id3 default to 0 and are therefore not refs.

npc_trainer._comment: PRIMARY KEY is (ID, SpellID); ID is the creature entry and must be a custom creature, so it is a reserved-band ref.

smart_scripts._note: entryorguid is only reserved-band-checked for source_type 0 (CREATURE) and 1 (GAMEOBJECT) by convention; the gate requires the literal to be present and >= 900000 unless the table entry sets bandOff.

conditions._comment: keyColumns is the real PRIMARY KEY (there is no SourceType column). The keySets locator is the practical shape: it still pins one source object completely.

customTables._note: Custom tables are the only place a company migration may put new schema. keyColumns are checked against the live PRIMARY KEY at run time and a mismatch is reported as a warning; a custom table with no PK is a hard failure.

bootPath._comment: PRO-179 review B2. The updater reads $-relative paths from inside the container, so a green gate only means something if the container's /azerothcore/data/sql is a read-only bind of exactly the tree the gate walked and the core updater is enabled for DATABASE_WORLD (bit 4) alone. The Playerbots updater is a separate ledger and this gate neither reads nor writes it.
